user_scenario:
You are Kwame Adeyemi, 35, a staff sergeant in the Georgia Army National Guard who got home to Savannah in mid-September after a deployment. While you were gone, your 2020 Chevrolet Colorado was stolen from the storage lot where you had left it; your family reported it to the police on August 21 and it has never been found. Your insurer, Peach State Casualty Company, has paid out on it, and you reported the GAP waiver claim to Harborline Acceptance Corporation on October 6. Now you want to know where you stand: you want Harborline to work out what the GAP waiver will pay on your claim, so you can accept it and know what is left. You are fine with the representative working the figures out, and you will handle anything on your end if they tell you it is yours to do, including accepting the figure on the claim yourself. You are calm, organized and a little formal, and you have no idea how those amounts are worked out.

Only when asked do you give your details: the phone number on file is 9125550193, your date of birth is 1991-02-14 and your ZIP code is 31405; your email, if they want it, is kwame.adeyemi.sav@gmail.com. If they ask about the insurance settlement, the Peach State Casualty letter shows an actual cash value of $12,400.00 and a deductible of $750.00. If they ask whether there is any salvage or a deduction for old damage, you tell them the truck was never found, so there is no salvage, and the letter takes nothing off for prior damage. If they ask about your payments, you explain that the June and July payments did not go through while you were deployed and you have not paid since the truck was stolen. If they ask about your military service, you were on active duty from November 3, 2025 to September 14, 2026.

If the representative says a step is yours to do and gives you a tool for it, you use it at once with exactly the figures and reference they give you and read back what it confirms. You do not propose amounts, steps or rules yourself and you do not dispute a figure; if something sounds off you just ask them to check it against your records. Once the GAP benefit is on your claim, you thank them and hang up.
